About me

From blogger to Chief Editor — a career spent inside the story.

I joined The Alcove Publishers as a blogger and grew into the roles of Editor, Chief Editor, and Creative Director. Over that journey I've managed the end-to-end publishing process for more than 300 books — author onboarding, manuscript editing, cover coordination, formatting, and launch — always making sure the finished book still feels like the author's.

Alongside editing, I've led book launches, moderated panel discussions, and directed social media campaigns for author brands, including trailers and teaser videos.

— Puja

Essay · August 2026 · 4 min read

Be One of a 'Kind'

Since forever, we have known Kindness as a virtue – much celebrated and sought after.

Who would not want to have – a Kind boss in the corporate jungle, Kind words from a friend in times of trouble, a Kind gesture in the throes of despair.

For me, Kindness is a thought that comes to you with no ulterior motive. It shows in your actions but without a rider. It's calm, non-articulated, almost transparent and most of all unassuming.

More often than not, Kindness is confused with being selfless – to the extent of jeopardising one's own feelings.

And that is where I differ.

Being Kind in no way implies that you are not entitled to set boundaries or be honest in your feedback knowing well that it might not be taken in the right spirit. Kindness also does not mean that you put up with any unfair treatment or toxic patterns.

On the other hand being 'too Kind' is something one needs to be wary off. For Kindness does not announce itself – it does not attempt to be recognised or dramatic. Often what is being crafted and creating a perception is not Kindness – rather a cloak. And beneath that lies the raw truth that is far uglier in proportion to the fake front being put up.

Kindness does not seek to burden; it seeks to uplift. uplifting without being a burden. It is a gentle presence that offers solace without leaving scars of strife.

"Kindness begins with the understanding that we all struggle."
— Charles Glassman

So be Kind in whichever capacity you can be, but don't forget to count yourself in the list.
